newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - SW Water profits seen rising.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - SW Water profits seen rising.

text.p: UK water and sewerage firm South West Water does not expect to sustain the 35 percent rise in pretax profits seen at the half year but profits will rise, finance director Ken Hill told Reuters in an interview.
"I do not think a 35 percent increase in PBT (profit before tax) is likely to occur at the end of this year," he said, nor in years immediately following. "But we are looking for profit increases."
The company turned in half-year pretax profits of 72.9 million stg, above expectations of 57-68 million stg, and paid out a dividend of 11.8 pence per share, up from 9.8 pence.
It said it hoped to raise the total dividend by 20 percent over a year ago and then reach eight percent real increases in the payout to shareholders.
"We are confident for the rest of the year," Hill said.

Hill said he did not think recent tax changes affecting some share buybacks would change company strategy, which it said in a statement was to use its buyback mandate only if it were in the interest of shareholders.
South West Water offered the interim dividend hike after two proposed bids against it from Severn Trent and Wessex Water were blocked by the UK government in October.
Hill said the company's strategy now was "to focus on the core business...and develop very carefully the strategy of the non-regulated businesses".
In addition, "we don't see an end to the cost savings," Hill said.
